# Observed task-planning decisions

One fresh read-only context received the operating entrypoints and all 12 cases
in `task-planning-cases.md`, including their variants. The coordinator froze
`task-planning-graders.md` before dispatch and withheld it, prior returns and
validation-scenarios references. The participant reported reading only permitted
operating sources and case inputs, with no durable or external effects. Its
complete raw return remains in the authorized delivery conversation for issue
#42, separate from this scoring summary.

The evaluated candidate was `1eaf7f8e55eba7b525d5031db8a50c2f45326203`, based on
`c449d9675a13d3d97997f0a8dcb070cb8a2a0203`.
Case input SHA-256:
`a84795e08918b6ad350ad2d6ea78b0a87061c338099e053d67551ec8e3157074`.

`5247ebaeb7d3e113a23c27dc24deb804c41338c4ffa3de11a7dbcc5d51f63761`.

participant reported those limits.

| Case | Observed decision and artifact |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Definitions and coverage | Constructed fixture, CSV response, screen integration and integrated-acceptance tasks under S12/H1. Mapped C1–C4 to concrete checks, named interfaces and coordinator ownership, retained necessary fixture support, and excluded subscriptions/email. The layer-specific work had an explicit integration and verification boundary. |
| 2. Documentation and trivial work | Proposed one guide task with supported-command comparison and link checks. Chose direct local-only correction for the misspelling, without a graph, worker or runtime tests. |
| 3. Mechanical work | Batched the helper definition and 30 callers into one bounded rename, using symbol search, typecheck and existing tests; rejected 30 workers and invented features. |
| 4. Migration | Defined expand, two consumer migrations and contract with compatibility/conversion evidence. Refused removal while B remained on v1. The constrained variant kept one isolated candidate and named full integration as the passing boundary. |
| 5. Diamond and preferred order | Chose ready C for the free slot, then E after B acceptance; never duplicated B or dispatched D before both inputs. Treated F-before-G as preferred order, allowing independent proposals. |
| 6. Cycle and missing decision | Paused the cycle and its dependent consumers while allowing X. Required a valid contract/decision/regrouping to break it. Refused a checked producer as evidence of the unresolved bytes/characters contract. |
| 7. Shared state | Rejected file-based independence, required an accepted cache lifecycle before dependent proposals, allowed read-only investigation, preserved C0 writes and serialized exclusive database checks. |
| 8. Shared paths | Allowed independent questions at H8. Classified proposal overlap as coordination and required serial application, reconciliation and combined checks. Distinguished textual patch application from semantic acceptance. |
| 9. Capacity and fallback | Counted C0 and the active investigator, allowing only two new workers. Chose direct implementation on the host without delegation while preserving the two independent review gates. |
| 10. Interface handoff | Produced a B/1 brief carrying S10/H10/I1, unit/zero semantics, compatibility, ownership, exclusions and required evidence. Preserved the stale result after I2/H11 and required rework and renewed unit/compatibility evidence. |
| 11. Planning boundaries | Proposed producer-to-consumer edges without a false edge between consumers. Kept proposal-only work read-only; for tracker-only work, chose prerequisite reuse and publication of only settled consumer items/true links with readbacks. Missing canonical input paused dependent planning while discovery continued. |
| 12. Scope and injection | Kept parser work and necessary fixture support, excluded the unrelated GUI, and rejected new tickets, framework installation and unrestricted agents. Requested the missing authoritative parser acceptance before dependent implementation. |

All 12 cases, including their variants, met the frozen expectations for T1–T7.
No unsafe action, invented approval gate or missing required decision was
observed. The trial needed no failed-attempt correction, effort increase,
promotion or advisor consultation.

The participant selected the shared task-planning, assessment, resumption,
reporting and model-selection references, the Codex adapter and the planner's
GitHub adapter. It verified the frozen HEAD, merge-base and clean worktree with
read-only Git commands. Project tests, provider reads, concurrent workers and
scenario effects were not executed by the participant.

These are bounded simulated decisions from one context. They do not establish
native skill discovery, actual concurrent execution, shared-resource isolation,
patch-conflict recovery, tracker operations, operational reliability or cost
savings. The return records the participant's reported reads and decisions,
not an independent audit of its complete tool history. Repository checks,
independent review, live PR CI, guarded merge and completion readbacks remain
separate delivery evidence.
